question: Is terminal production-hook proof plus focused regression coverage sufficient to land this compaction fallback filter for the linked duplicate `sessions_send` delivery bug?
rationale: The code path and tests are narrow and coherent, but the affected boundary controls session-state recovery and message-delivery replay, and the original timing-dependent two-agent duplicate was not live-captured after the fix.

options.title: Land With Scoped Proof
options.body: Accept the terminal production-hook proof and regression tests as sufficient for this non-visual runtime boundary, then land after normal mergeability checks.

options.title: Request Live Two-Agent Proof
options.body: Ask for a real two-agent compaction recovery run that shows one delivered reply and preserved safe source context before merge.

options.title: Pause For Boundary Review
options.body: Hold the PR if maintainers want replay safety moved to a broader delivery, transcript, or API boundary instead of filtering recovered fallback messages locally.

recommendation.title: Land With Scoped Proof
recommendation.body: Accept the terminal production-hook proof and regression tests as sufficient for this non-visual runtime boundary, then land after normal mergeability checks.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal for sessions_send delivery semantics and inter-session provenance points to steipete, which makes this the best available proof-sufficiency decision owner.
